src.q: Moxifloxacin has been shown to prolong the QTc interval on the electrocardiogram in some patients.
Fluoroquinolones affect the QT interval to varying degrees but have very rarely caused torsades de pointes.

notes: Batch AB (metronidazole, tinidazole, clindamycin, moxifloxacin, levofloxacin, mebendazole), 2026-10-17. All 607 quotes checked FOUND with lib/text.mjs quoteFound. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). REUSED SOURCES (not redefined here): mhra-dsu-2024-01-fluoroquinolones, mhra-dsu-2018-11-fq-aortic, mhra-dsu-2020-12-fq-valve, mhra-dsu-2023-09-fq-suicidal (batch E); sps-qt-commonly-used (batch P). NO UK PRODUCT: tinidazole. emc search by ingredient and by trade name returned nothing; the emc page linked from the clinic monograph (product 1066) now returns 404; the MHRA Products search index has no tinidazole document of any type (by name or content); SPS and BUMPS have no tinidazole page. Marked no-uk-product, no rules, and not added to the nitroimidazole group (no UK source to cite), so the metronidazole nitroimidazole allergy rule will not catch tinidazole unless another source adds it. FORMULATION PROXY: the clinic's clindamycin 100 mg vaginal capsule (ovule) has no UK SmPC; the UK SPC for clindamycin 100 mg pessaries (PL 35533/0315, MHRA Products) was used and this is stated in the formulation note. Its 4.8 table is garbled by the PDF layout, so common vs uncommon cannot be split exactly (item marked detail and says so). Clindamycin systemic rules (warfarin, CYP3A4, nephrotoxic, renal monitoring) are scoped to the capsule formulation only. METRONIDAZOLE SOURCES: the clinic-linked 200 mg tablet SmPC (emc 12348) has no renal/hepatic text, so renal and hepatic content comes from a second 200 mg tablet SmPC (emc 13521) and the suspension SmPC (emc 101002). emc 6690 (another 200 mg/5 ml suspension) was read and matches 101002; not used. CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules): (1) Metronidazole 500 mg tablet SmPC (emc 13016) section 4.3 lists first-trimester use for trichomoniasis/bacterial vaginosis, breastfeeding within 12-24 h of a single high (2 g) dose, and Cockayne syndrome as contraindications; the 200 mg tablet and suspension SmPCs do not (they say 'should not be given in pregnancy or lactation unless essential'). Cockayne syndrome: 500 mg SmPC contraindicated vs 200 mg tablet SmPCs 'should not be used unless benefit outweighs risk' (avoid) vs suspension SmPC 'used after careful benefit-risk assessment' (caution). (2) Metronidazole breastfeeding: SmPCs avoid / stop 12-24 h after high dose vs SPS 'compatible', no interruption even after 2 g doses, with infant monitoring. (3) Metronidazole hepatic encephalopathy: one tablet SmPC 'should be reduced to one third' vs suspension SmPC 'may be reduced'. (4) Metronidazole interactions differ by SmPC: carbamazepine and tacrolimus appear only in the suspension SmPCs; QT-prolonging drugs only in the tablet SmPCs. (5) Moxifloxacin and levofloxacin pregnancy: SmPC contraindicated vs BUMPS 'can be used if recommended by your doctor' (another antibiotic usually tried first). (6) Mebendazole pregnancy: SmPC contraindicated vs BUMPS 'can be used' (hygiene measures first if preferred, maybe delay to about 12 weeks). (7) Clindamycin inflammatory bowel disease: vaginal cream SmPC contraindicated vs pessary SmPC caution; capsule SmPC caution for history of GI disease/colitis. MAPPING DECISIONS: metronidazole + alcohol mapped to condition alcohol-dependence (level avoid, 'advised not to take alcohol'), as other batches did for alcohol. Metronidazole was NOT added to qt-prolonging (SmPCs only report QT prolongation mainly with other QT drugs, frequency not known); its QT interaction rule is level info. Moxifloxacin 4.3 'electrolyte disturbances, particularly uncorrected hypokalaemia' mapped to hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia (both contraindicated). Moxifloxacin 'agents containing bivalent or trivalent cations' and levofloxacin 'preparations containing divalent or trivalent cations' mapped to iron-preparation, magnesium-preparation and aluminium-magnesium-hydroxide; calcium excluded because both SmPCs say calcium has no/minimal effect. Moxifloxacin potassium-lowering 'laxatives and enemas [high doses]' mapped to group:laxative (concern says high doses). Levofloxacin renal bands: 50-20 mL/min = min 20, max 50 inclusive; 19-10 = min 10, max 20; <10 = max 10. Mebendazole-metronidazole avoid rule is only on mebendazole (the metronidazole SmPCs do not mention it). New group lincosamide (clindamycin) created for the clindamycin/lincomycin allergy rule. NOT USED: MHRA DSU 'Moxifloxacin: increased risk of life-threatening liver reactions' (2011) is superseded by the 2024 fluoroquinolone restriction. No SPS breastfeeding page exists for clindamycin, quinolones or mebendazole (searched); breastfeeding for those comes from SmPCs only. No BUMPS clindamycin leaflet exists (404). AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent second check, AB; log in audit/AB-AC.md): tinidazole no-uk-product CONFIRMED (emc search for tinidazole and the clinic trade name: no results; old emc product 1066 returns 404; MHRA Products search index, product name and full text: no tinidazole product, only other products that mention it). Metronidazole: the four 500 mg tablet SmPC (emc 13016) rules that are stricter than the 200 mg tablet and suspension SmPCs (Cockayne contraindication, first-trimester contraindication for trichomoniasis/BV, breastfeeding stop after single 2 g dose, epilepsy caution) and their section items are now scoped to metronidazole-tab, with the qualifier in the concern; the suspension follows its own SmPC. metronidazole:hepatic:severe dose -> info (no action is stated for advanced hepatic insufficiency itself; the one-third dose applies to hepatic encephalopathy, which has its own rule); hepatic-encephalopathy rule effect hepatotoxicity removed (accumulation, not liver injury). Clindamycin: IBD caution item reworded so it no longer implies caution for the cream (cream 4.3 contraindicates a history of IBD); 7-fold absorption note now quoted. Moxifloxacin and levofloxacin iron rules now use the ingredient id iron (the SmPCs say agents/preparations containing iron), so they also fire for iron products outside group iron-preparation (e.g. iron-polymaltose-b-complex). Mebendazole: age 1-2 rule caution -> avoid (4.4 Not recommended in the treatment of children under 2 years); new hepatic info rule.
